header.running_head: Finding a Change in Oneself at the Death of an Elder

In a narration discussing the Hijrah of Rasulullaah ﷺ, Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "I saw Rasulullaah ﷺ the day he came to us in Madinah. I have never seen a day better and brighter than the day Rasulullaah ﷺ entered Madinah. I also saw him the day he passed away and have never seen a day worse or darker than that day."[^2]
The Statement of Hadhrat Abu Talha (RA) the Day Hadhrat Umar (RA) Passed away

Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that when the consultative assembly (appointed by Hadhrat Umar (RA) before his death) assembled, Hadhrat Abu Talha (RA) saw what they were doing (each one wishing the Khilaafah for the next) and said, "More than my fear that you should all be aspiring for the Khilaafah is my fear that you should all want to pass it on another. By Allaah! Every Muslim home has suffered a deficiency in its religious and worldly affairs by the death of Umar (RA)."[^3]
Honouring the Weak and Poor Muslims
Rasulullaah ﷺ Honours the Poor Muslims

Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA) narrates that they were six Muslims with Rasulullaah ﷺ when the Mushrikeen said (to Rasulullaah ﷺ), "Drive these people away from you." They then went on to belittle these Sahabah (RA) (indicating that they as wealthy people could not sit with these poor men). The Sahabah (RA) included Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA), Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA), a Sahabi form the Banu Hudhayl tribe, Hadhrat Bilaal (RA) and two other Sahabah (RA) whose names the narrator had forgotten. When Rasulullaah ﷺ started to consider the request, Allaah revealed the verse:

blocks.arabic_text: وَلَا تَطْرُدِ الَّذِيْنَ يَدْعُوْنَ رَبَّهُمْ بِالْغَدٰوةِ وَالْعَشِيِّ يُرِيْدُوْنَ وَجْهَهٗ
blocks.text: ... Do not drive away those (poor Sahabah (RA)) who call (worship) their Rabb morning and evening, seeking His pleasure...[^4]

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) reports that a group of the Quraysh once passed by Rasulullaah ﷺ when he was in the company of some poor Muslims such as Hadhrat Suhayb (RA), Hadhrat Bilaal (RA), Hadhrat Khabbaab (RA) and Hadhrat Ammaar (RA). The Mushrikeen said, "O Muhammad! Are you content with the likes of these men from your people? Should we become followers of these people?
